```{python}
#| output: false
import os

import pandas as pd
import yaml

cfg = yaml.safe_load(open("configs/settings.yaml"))

mig_dir = cfg["remi_migration_dir"]
remi_base_year = cfg["remi_base_year"]


def load_remi_migration(file_path):
    """Read a REMI migration workbook's single 'Total Migrants' row (in
    thousands, for the combined region) into a long [year, net_migrants] frame."""
    df = pd.read_excel(file_path, sheet_name="All", header=5)
    s = df.drop(columns=["Category", "Units"]).iloc[0] * 1000
    s.index = s.index.astype(int)
    return s.rename("net_migrants").rename_axis("year").reset_index()


mig_frames = []
for mig_file in cfg["remi_migration_files"]:
    file_path = os.path.join(mig_dir, mig_file["filename"])
    df = load_remi_migration(file_path)
    df["name"] = mig_file["name"]
    mig_frames.append(df)
migration = pd.concat(mig_frames, ignore_index=True)

scenario_names = [mig_file["name"] for mig_file in cfg["remi_migration_files"]]

# History is identical across scenario files through remi_base_year, so keep
# a single historical series and one forecast series per migration scenario.
mig_hist = (
    migration.loc[migration["year"] <= remi_base_year]
    .drop_duplicates("year")[["year", "net_migrants"]]
    .assign(name="History")
)
mig_forecast = migration.loc[migration["year"] > remi_base_year]
mig_all = pd.concat([mig_hist, mig_forecast], ignore_index=True)

# Average annual net migrants by period, split at remi_base_year like the plot above.
periods = [
    ("2000s", 2001, 2009),
    ("2010s", 2010, 2019),
    ("2020s", 2020, 2024),
    ("2025-2039", 2025, 2039),
    ("2040-2060", 2040, 2060),
]
period_avgs = [
    mig_all.loc[(mig_all["year"] >= start) & (mig_all["year"] <= end)]
    .groupby("name")["net_migrants"]
    .mean()
    .rename(label)
    for label, start, end in periods
]
period_avg_table = pd.concat(period_avgs, axis=1).T[["History"] + scenario_names]

ojs_define(data=mig_all, base_year=remi_base_year)
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
maxYear = Math.ceil(d3.max(allData, d => d.year) / 5) * 5
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// History always shown; the scenario checkboxes only toggle the forecast lines.
scenarioNames = Array.from(new Set(allData.map(d => d.name))).filter(n => n !== "History").sort()
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
filtered = allData.filter(d =>
  (d.name === "History" || selectedScenarios.includes(d.name)) &&
  d.year >= yearFrom &&
  d.year <= yearTo
)
```

# Notes

- **History**: historical net migration input to the REMI economic model, identical across all scenarios through `{python} remi_base_year`.
- Scenario forecasts:
  - **v.3.4**: Default REMI forecast released August 2026
  - **Low**: Uses the "Census Low" international migration scenario
  - **High** Uses the "Census High" international migration scenario
  - **Zero_Intl_Mig**: Assumes zero international migration
